title: Well interference policy approved with stronger data sharing
subtitle: Mannheim water capacity update, 2027 water staffing needs, and a consultant contract increase for the water supply strategy.
overview: Regional Council held a special meeting on water. It endorsed a revised Well Interference Policy and the Appeal Committee terms of reference, after adding stronger data-sharing rules. Well owners who make a claim will now automatically receive the investigation records and data with the technical evaluation, and the Appeal Committee and the appellant will see the same information before a hearing. Monitoring data from nearby wells must also be provided. {{vote:m2}}

Council also approved a $440,000 increase to the consultant contract for the Water Supply Strategy Update, bringing the total to $1,789,434.17 plus taxes {{vote:m3}}. The extra work stems from the Mannheim water capacity constraint. Staff said a short list of long-term options, including surface water such as a pipeline, will come back by the end of 2026.

Staff reported that the extra 15 L/s borrowed from the Wilmot Centre Wellfield will no longer be needed after January 2027, and that revised plans for the CAM2 West project and the Parkway Wells are expected to save money and bring water online sooner. Council received a report on 2027 water staffing and asked staff to look at offsetting new positions. The Regional Chair said the last scheduled special water meeting is in October.

decisions.detail: Council amended the policy so appellants automatically receive investigation records, data and nearby monitoring well data with the technical evaluation, and receive the same information as the Appeal Committee before a hearing.
Council endorsed the revised Well Interference Policy and the Appeal Committee terms of reference, with the amended sections 4.5 and 8.

decisions.item: Water Supply Strategy Update contract increase
decisions.detail: Council increased the CIMA Canada contract by $440,000 plus taxes, for a total of $1,789,434.17 plus taxes.

debate: Delegates from rural and agricultural groups and a well owner said well owners bear high costs when wells fail and should not be treated as complainants. They asked for fair compensation and for well monitoring data to be shared with residents.

A citizens' groundwater group asked for guaranteed advance review time, an independent technical expert, and hard-stop pumping triggers at low water levels. Staff said triggers already exist for the Wilmot Centre Wellfield, with monitoring beyond permit requirements. They said the consultant is bound by conflict-of-interest rules and goes out with a well technician.

On the data-sharing amendment, staff asked for flexibility so residents are not given decades of monitoring data. The wording was changed to a relevant time range, with more data available on request, and staff had no concerns.

On the contract increase, one councillor questioned the cost growth, the lack of visible results and the scope's focus on the integrated urban system. Others asked whether this would be the last increase. Staff said over half the work was done before the constraint, the update re-baselined the models, and a small contingency remains. Council asked for the total cost including contingencies.

On 2027 water staffing, some councillors raised affordability and asked for offsets through attrition and review of positions that were temporary. Staff said operator shortages, aging assets and new infrastructure drive the need for about 10 positions.
